To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) revenue sharing affects the allocation of free agency players to teams by altering team rankings of ability to pay, and (2) revenue sharing affects player salaries by altering the distribution of salary offers among teams.

(1) pooled revenue sharing will not alter team ability to pay rankings, but will alter the allocation of free-agent players, and (2) traditional gate revenue sharing will alter both team ability to pay and player allocation rankings.

(i) the imposition of a revenue sharing system can affect the allocation and salaries of free agents to teams; (ii) the imposition of revenue pooling does not affect ability to pay rankings of teams; and (iii) the imposition of gate revenue sharing can affect ability to pay, depending on the closeness of gate revenues between teams.

the effect of revenue sharing on the allocation of players to teams.
the effects of revenue sharing on the distribution of player talent among teams in professional sports.
the effect of revenue sharing on the distribution of player wages.

revenue sharing can be an effective means to reduce the salary dispersion among players in a professional sport league.
